example_summary: Ankur received ₹ 5 lacs for allowing a film shoot on his Kerala agricultural land and claimed it as exempt agricultural income.
source_provision:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Agricultural Income & Exemption

| Statutory Provision | Core Condition / Nexus Test | Judicial Precedent / Benchmark | Tax Treatment / Exemption Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 10(1)** | Agricultural income derived from land situated in India is totally exempt from income-tax. | **CIT v. Raja Benoy Kumar Sahas Roy (SC)**: Requires direct nexus with agricultural operations. | **100% Exempt** from total income under Chapter III. |
| **Section 2(1A)(a)** | Rent or revenue derived from land situated in India and used for agricultural purposes. | **B. Nagi Reddi v. CIT (Madras HC)**: Income from film shooting on land lacks agricultural nexus. | **Taxable as Income from Other Sources** / Non-agricultural. |


### Core Statutory Rules & Legal Tests

- **Basic & Subsequent Operations**: Agricultural income under Section 2(1A) mandates human labour and skill applied to the land itself (tilling, sowing, planting) along with subsequent cultivation operations.
- **Direct Nexus Requirement**: Any commercial exploitation of agricultural land (such as film shooting, leasing for exhibitions, or non-agricultural storage) that does not exploit the vegetative or productive capacity of the soil is strictly excluded from agricultural income.


> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Judicial Benchmark on Film Shooting**: The Madras High Court and Supreme Court have categorically ruled that amounts received for permitting film shooting on agricultural land are commercial receipts, not agricultural income, because the income has no direct nexus with agricultural produce or operations.


> [!WARNING]
> **Tax Trap**: Merely holding land that possesses agricultural characteristics or is classified as rural agricultural land in revenue records is insufficient; the actual source of the receipt must be derived from agricultural activity.
